summary.text: Ozone depletion is the thinning of Earth's stratospheric ozone layer seen since the late 1970s, along with a much larger springtime loss around the polar regions.
Manufactured chemicals such as CFCs and halons are mixed up into the stratosphere, where they release halogen atoms that speed the breakdown of ozone into oxygen.
It matters because the ozone layer blocks harmful UVB light that causes skin cancer and cataracts, and that worry led to the 1987 Montreal Protocol.

facts.label: Ozone hole
facts.value: The springtime ozone loss over the south pole

facts.label: One chlorine atom
facts.value: Reacts with about 100,000 ozone molecules on average

facts.label: Worst Antarctic loss
facts.value: Up to 70 percent of the ozone column

facts.label: Projected full recovery
facts.value: By 2045 under current rules, says the UN

items.prompt: Only a small amount of chlorine reaches the stratosphere, yet it does huge damage to ozone. Why?

options.label: Each atom is reused to destroy ozone again and again
Chlorine blocks sunlight that ozone needs to form
Chlorine attaches to ozone and drags it to the ground
Chlorine heats the air until ozone boils away

items.explain: Chlorine works as a catalyst: it is freed to repeat its cycle, so a single atom reacts with about 100,000 ozone molecules on average.

items.prompt: CFCs leak out of old fridges at ground level. How do they end up high in the stratosphere?

options.label: Rain carries them up as it evaporates
Churning air mixes them up before they settle
Sunlight splits them into lighter pieces
Volcanoes blast them up during eruptions

items.explain: After being emitted, these compounds are carried up by turbulent mixing, which moves them much faster than they can settle.

items.prompt: Why would a thinner ozone layer lead to more cases of skin cancer?

options.label: Ozone itself is absorbed through the skin
Less ozone makes the air near the ground hotter
More harmful UVB light reaches the ground
The chemicals involved settle onto the skin

items.explain: The ozone layer stops harmful UVB wavelengths from passing through the atmosphere, and those wavelengths cause skin cancer and sunburn.

items.prompt: Atom for atom, how does bromine compare with chlorine as an ozone destroyer?

options.label: Weaker, and also far less common
Exactly as strong, and just as common
Weaker, but far more common in the air
More destructive, but much scarcer in the air

items.explain: Bromine is even more efficient than chlorine per atom, but there is much less bromine in the atmosphere.

items.prompt: In which season is the drop in ozone over the poles largest?

options.label: Midwinter
Spring
Midsummer
Late autumn

items.explain: Besides the overall thinning, a much larger decrease happens in springtime around the polar regions, which over the south pole is called the ozone hole.

items.prompt: Several radicals destroy ozone. Which ones has human activity drastically increased in the stratosphere?

options.label: Hydroxyl and nitric oxide
Hydroxyl and chlorine
Chlorine and bromine
Nitric oxide and bromine

items.explain: Most stratospheric hydroxyl and nitric oxide is natural, but human activity has drastically raised chlorine and bromine levels.
